findings.title: Backfill assumes an orders.id column exists and will fail if the table uses a different primary key
findings.evidence: The batched UPDATE selects and filters rows via an unguarded id reference, so on any supported PostgreSQL deployment where orders has no id column the DO block errors and aborts the migration instead of being idempotent.
findings.recommendation: Avoid hard-coding a non-guarded id column in the migration. Either backfill with a plain guarded UPDATE without batching, or batch using PostgreSQL row identifiers such as ctid, or first check the schema and only run the id-based batch when the column exists.
